newsitem.title: USA: "Progress" toward ending polio by 2000 - official.
newsitem.headline: "Progress" toward ending polio by 2000 - official.

text.p: Cases of polio fell by 43 percent worlwide last year in what the U.S. secretary of health said on Thursday was "extraordinary progress" toward eradicating the disease by 2000.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said there were 3,997 confirmed polio cases reported globally in 1996, down from 7,032 in 1995, and 155 countries reported no polio cases last year, compared with 150 countries in 1995.
No confirmed cases were reported in the Americas last year, the agency said.

There were 1,898 confirmed cases in the Africa and 1,116 in Southeast Asia last year. The CDC said cases in Southeast Asia fell 67 percent in 1996. Health officials said national immunization days were largely responsible for the decline.

"The biggest campaigns that come to mind are the ones that were conducted in India in December 1995 and January 1996, where they covered 127 million children less than five years of age," Dr. Roland Sutter of the CDC said.
Donna Shalala, secretary of health and human services, said the latest figures showed "extraordinary progress toward achieving the global eradication of polio by the year 2000."
